steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: E-commerce allows businesses to sell online 24/7, reaching a global market with lower overhead costs than a physical shop.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Digital communication (email, video conferencing, social media) speeds up decision-making and enables remote/flexible working.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Automation and robotics increase productivity and consistency but reduce unskilled jobs and require high capital investment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: EPOS (Electronic Point of Sale) tracks sales in real time, manages stock levels automatically, and provides data for marketing decisions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two ways e-commerce has changed how businesses sell to customers. | Analyse the impact of automation on a manufacturing business and its workers. | Evaluate whether a small retail business should invest in an online store.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When evaluating technology, always consider both the benefits AND the costs/risks - no technology is purely positive. Use stakeholder analysis: technology may benefit owners (lower costs) but harm workers (job losses). Link technology to competitiveness: businesses that fail to adapt risk losing market share.
